full_judgment: 3. The defendants-petitioners contested the above suit by filing written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that Shihamul Haque, his father Anamul Haq and mother Tahera Sogra Begum, were the inhabitants of Bardwan district in India. After they settled in the then East Pakistan in 1950 migrating from India, Chaturi Tanti along with Shibulal, Buttu, Surjagaya and Nathan "Fanti proposed to exchange their lands including suit land of the above mouza Chandana with the land of Shamsul Hoque, Enamul Hoque and Tahera Sogra Begum at Bardwan. Accordingly, a deed of agreement was duly executed which was registered on 30.10.1963 and pursuant to the above agreement the parties handed over possession of their respective lands to each other acknowledging delivery of possession. Embargo having been created upon the Hindus to transfer their properties by registered deed of conveyances on promulgation of Defence of Pakistan Rules, several powers of attorney were given to each other by either the sides on the basis or which deeds of exchange were executed in Bardawan in India. By one of such deeds of exchange dated 09.08.1968 executed in India Tahera Sogra Begun exchanged 1.36 acres of her lands at Bardwan with .89 acre land of Chaturi and Nathuni Tanti of mouza Chandana including the suit land. Bhatu Tanti, Chaturi Tanti and 3 others made joint declaration before the Notary Public in Calcutta on 15.07.1968 and 12.08.1968 confirming the above exchange of their lands of mouza Chandana including the suit land. The facts of the execution and registration of the above agreement to exchange in the year 1963, the irrevocable power of attorney and the exchange deeds were duly certified by the Magistrate,. First Class, Alipur, West Bengal, India on 17.07.1968 and 10.09.1968. Shihamul Haque applied to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka praying for permission to execute and register the deed of exchange under the authority of the general power of attorney executed in his favour whereupon Exchange Case No. 35/69-70 was started. Shibulal Tanti, Chaturi Tanti and others filed an objection in the above exchange case contending, inter-alia, they did not enter into any such agreement nor did they exchange their properties. They further contended that the deed of exchange is fraudulent and powers of attorney are collusive and were vitiated by coercion, threat and intimidation. Shibulal Tanti also filed Title Suit No. 27 of 1971 in the 1st Court' of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against Shihamul Haque and others challenging the deed of egret:- Mont for exchange, powers of attorney as well as the deed of exchange but the suit was dismissed for non-prosecution. Subsequently he prayed for restoration of the suit which was rejected by the order dated 08.06.1972. After that Shibulal Tanti filed Title Suit No. 150 of 1972 in the same court against Shihamul Haque and others seeking same declarations as made in the previous suit and then prayed for amendment which was rejected as the suit filed earlier was dismissed. Against the order of rejection, Shibulal Tanti filed Civil Revision No. 315 of 1977 and Civil Revision No. 1372 of 1977 on more or less similar grounds. Then both the above Rules were discharged on the basis of prayers of Shibulal Tanti to the effect that they did not want to press the Rules. Alter disposal of the above suits/revisions Shihamul Haque applied to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka to proceed with the Exchange Case No. 35 of 1969-70. After snaking necessary enquiry and completing all the formalities the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka executed and registered the deed of exchange (Settlement) on 16.06.1980 transferring 7.12 acres of land of mouza Chandana in favour of Shihamul Haque. Soon after on the basis of the above deed of exchange Shihamul Haque started Mutation Appeal Case No. 13 of 1981 in the office of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka, praying for canceling the earlier mutation in the name of the plaintiffs-respondents and got the mutation cancelled. Against the order of cancellation, the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka in Appeal Case No. 8 of 1982 set aside the order of the Additional Deputy commissioner (Dhaka). Shihamul Haque moved the Board of Land Administration and having been unsuccessful filed Writ Petition No. 154 of 1989 in which the Rule was made absolute with the observation that the question of title and validity of the, deed of exchange could be decided only by the civil court. The defendants have been possessing the suit land along with other lands by cultivating and growing crops therein through bargadars, namely, Kamal's mother and her son-in-law.
